sections.h2: Where is Skagit County and what shapes its property values?
sections.html:
Skagit County is in the Puget Sound region of Washington, and Mount Vernon is both the county seat and its largest city. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate counts 132,975 residents across about 1,730 square miles of land, which gives the county a density of roughly 75 people per square mile.

Four cities (Anacortes, Burlington, Mount Vernon and Sedro-Woolley) and four towns (Concrete, Hamilton, La Conner and Lyman) are incorporated. The county was formed in 1883 from the southern part of Whatcom County. Its land runs from the broad Skagit River valley, a center for tulips, blueberries and strawberries, out to Fidalgo and Guemes islands and east into the Cascade foothills, so a house in Skagit County might sit on a city lot, a farm parcel or a island shoreline.

The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures put the median owner-occupied home at $545,100, and 70.1% of housing units are owner-occupied. Median household income is $89,263. About 25.0% of residents are 65 or older, a share that makes the county's senior exemption (covered below) relevant to a large group of owners.

sections.h2: Which Skagit County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Three offices split the work. The Assessor sets values, establishes levies and approves exemptions. The Treasurer sends bills and collects payment. The Board of Equalization is the body that hears value appeals.

OfficeWhat it doesWhere and how to reach it
TreasurerCollects tax, takes payments, answers late-payment questions700 S. 2nd Street, Room 205, Mount Vernon, WA 98273; 360-416-1750; mail to PO Box 518
AssessorValues property, sets levies, approves exemptions360-416-1780; assessor@skagitcountywa.gov
Board of EqualizationHears appeals of assessed value700 S. 2nd Street, Room 100, Mount Vernon; clerk at 360-416-1126

Source: Skagit County Treasurer, Skagit County Assessor FAQ and Board of Equalization guide.

A satellite office in Concrete (45770 A Main Street) also takes tax payments from the east end of the county, though it accepts cash, check or money order only.

sections.h2: When are Skagit County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Skagit County taxes are due in two installments, April 30 and October 31, and a bill under $50 must be paid in full by April 30 (RCW 84.56.020). The second installment for 2026 was due October 31, 2026, so the next date on the calendar is April 30, 2027.

The county lists these ways to pay:

  • In person at the Treasurer in Mount Vernon with cash, check, money order or card.
  • In a drop box at 700 S. 2nd Street, either at the west end of the horseshoe parking lot or on the second floor outside Room 205 (check or money order only).
  • By phone at 1-866-791-3392, where the processor adds a $3.95 convenience fee plus 2.35% on debit and credit cards or $1.00 on checks.
  • By auto-pay, which withdraws from a U.S. checking or savings account on April 30 and October 31, or the full year on April 30. Enrollment forms are due April 15 for the spring withdrawal and October 15 for the fall one.

Mail carries a trap. The Treasurer warns that the Postal Service no longer guarantees a same-day postmark, and a payment must be postmarked by the due date to count as timely. Mail early, or use a drop box.

sections.h2: What does a late Skagit County tax payment cost?
sections.html:
In Skagit County, interest on a late payment is figured on the full-year tax and starts May 1. Call the Treasurer at 360-416-1750 for the exact payoff figure before you send money.

State law sets the rates. For taxes levied from 2023 on, residential property with four or fewer units and manufactured homes carries 9% annual interest and no penalty. Other real property and personal property carry 12% interest, plus a 3% penalty on tax delinquent on June 1 and another 8% on December 1 (RCW 84.56.020).

A few waivers exist. If the county failed to send the notice, the treasurer must waive interest and penalties. A taxpayer who misses one payment on a personal residence because of a spouse's death, or on a parent's or stepparent's residence after that parent's death, can get interest and penalties waived by telling the treasurer within 60 days of the due date (RCW 84.56.025). The treasurer may also offer payment agreements and accept partial payments, with money applied to the oldest year first.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Skagit County assessment?
sections.html:
You appeal to the Skagit County Board of Equalization, and the deadline is printed on your Notice of Value. For 2026 values the deadline was Monday, October 26, 2026, so it has passed. That date applied even to owners whose value did not change and who received no notice.

The 2026 notices reflect market value on January 1, 2026 and set the tax payable in 2027. Washington law allows a petition by July 1 or 30 days after the notice was mailed, whichever is later (RCW 84.40.038). The board can waive a late filing if the petition follows within a reasonable time and shows good cause, such as a serious illness or a postal delay documented by the Postal Service. Call the clerk at 360-416-1126 if you think you qualify.

Here is how a hearing works in Skagit County:

  • You get 10 minutes, the Assessor gets 10 minutes, and you then respond.
  • The Assessor's value is presumed correct, and you must show an error with clear, cogent and convincing evidence (RCW 84.40.0301).
  • Strong evidence includes comparable sales near the valuation date, contractor repair estimates and independent appraisals. Listings do not count.
  • Extra documents must arrive 21 business days before the hearing.
  • The county says the whole process can take 6 to 12 months.

Tax amount, personal hardship and the size of the increase are not valid grounds. A losing owner has 30 days to take the case to the Washington State Board of Tax Appeals. The Assessor's next reinspection cycle starts in the Mount Vernon School District, using street-level imagery along with aerial views, so owners there may see value changes tied to updated property records.

sections.h2: Which relief programs help Skagit County homeowners?
sections.html:
The main program is the Senior and Persons with Disability Property Tax Exemption. The Assessor's page says it covers homeowners age 61 or older, owners with disabilities, and veterans with a 40% VA rating, and that the income limit rises to $78,000 in 2027.

Eligibility uses combined disposable income, which is adjusted gross income plus certain untaxed income such as Social Security, pensions and annuities, counted for everyone who owns and lives in the home. You may subtract a standard deduction of $7,500 per person (you, plus a spouse or domestic partner) or your actual qualifying costs, such as prescriptions, Medicare premiums and care costs. New for 2027, up to $6,000 of rental income from living space in your home can also be subtracted. Call 360-416-1780 to run the worksheet with staff.

Other relief to know about: a tax statement must include a notice about both the exemption and the state deferral program (RCW 84.56.020). If a fire or other event destroys part or all of a property, you can claim a value reduction within three years of the damage (RCW 84.70.010).

sections.h2: What special charges appear on a Skagit County tax bill?
sections.html:
Some line items are special assessments, not property taxes, and they fall outside the 1% limit on regular levies. The Assessor does not set them. Each district or program sets its own budget and spreads it by acreage, value or another method.

  • Diking and drainage districts maintain dikes, ditches and pump stations in their area.
  • The Clean Water Assessment funds the county's Clean Water Program, which targets bacterial pollution including Samish Bay shellfish beds, septic repairs and water monitoring.
  • The County Drainage Utility pays for drainage and stormwater work such as pump stations, piping, tide gates and ditches.

Two houses with the same assessed value can pay different totals because each sits in a different mix of city, school, fire and library districts. The Assessor's Levy Trends tool shows the levies that apply to a given address.

sections.h2: How does unpaid tax affect selling a Skagit County house?
sections.html:
Unpaid Skagit County tax has to be cleared from the sale proceeds or the buyer inherits the problem, so ask the Treasurer for a payoff covering every year owed before you accept an offer. Remember that interest keeps accruing monthly until the day it is paid.

Washington also charges a real estate excise tax on sales, due to the county treasurer on the date of sale whether or not the deed is recorded that day. Usually the seller pays. For sales beginning January 1, 2027, the Department of Revenue lists graduated state rates of 1.1% on the part of the price up to $551,000, 1.28% from $551,000 to $1,551,000, 2.75% from there to $3,051,000 and 3.0% above that. A local rate is added, so ask the Treasurer for the full amount.

Waiting has limits. Once taxes are three years past delinquency, the treasurer must issue certificates of delinquency and begin foreclosure (RCW 84.64.050). An income-qualified owner living in the home may qualify for a waiver of interest and penalties shortly before that three-year mark if foreclosure is under way (RCW 84.56.020).

faqs.q: When are Skagit County property taxes due?
faqs.a: April 30 and October 31, with the full year due April 30 if the bill is under $50. The 2026 second half was due October 31, 2026, so the next due date is April 30, 2027. Late payments carry interest from May 1 on the full-year amount.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my 2026 Skagit County value?
faqs.a: The published deadline was Monday, October 26, 2026, and it has passed. The Board of Equalization may waive a late filing for good cause, such as serious illness or documented postal delay. Call the clerk at 360-416-1126 to ask, and bring your Notice of Value or parcel number.

faqs.q: What interest rate applies to late Skagit County tax?
faqs.a: For a home with four or fewer units, interest is 9% per year with no penalty. Other property pays 12% per year plus a 3% penalty after June 1 and an additional 8% after December 1. Call the Treasurer at 360-416-1750 for the figure on your parcel.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Skagit County property tax question?
faqs.a: Call the Treasurer at 360-416-1750 for bills, payments and payoff amounts, and the Assessor at 360-416-1780 for values and exemptions. The Board of Equalization clerk is at 360-416-1126 for appeals.

faqs.q: How long can Skagit County property tax stay unpaid before foreclosure?
faqs.a: The treasurer must start foreclosure by certificate of delinquency once taxes are three years past delinquency, and no certificate may be filed if the delinquent tax is $100 or less (RCW 84.64.050). Sell or pay well before that point, since interest builds every month.
